simple.meaning: רָבַךְ (râbak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to soak (bread in oil).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.

definitions.full: H7246. rabak [ רָבַךְ ] verb mix, stir (Arabic mix, mingle ; Late Hebrew רְבִיכָא ᵑ7 רְבִיכָה, [for Biblical Hebrew מֻרְבֶּכֶת ], (dough) mixed , or stirred ); — Hoph`al Participle f. as technical term in sacrifice, always of סֹלֶת well mixed , מֻרְבֶּכֶת Lev 6:14 ; 7:12 , הִימּרְבָּ֑כֶת 1Chr 23:29 .

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘This is the law of the meal offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before Yahweh, before the altar.
If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mixed with oil.

for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
